Receipts — neatHack build plan
Oct 10, 2026 · @dd
Pitch
Receipts resolves "debited but not credited" complaints end to end, and is not allowed to tell the customer anything it cannot prove from a trace span.
The four rules it lives by:
1. Every claim needs a receipt. Each factual claim in an outgoing reply must point to the tool span that proves it. A deterministic verifier blocks the send otherwise.
2. Receipts expire. A claim about a balance or status is only valid if its read happened after the last action that could have changed it. Stale proof means re-check before sending.
3. Sources disagree, the agent decides who to trust. Sender bank, switch and beneficiary bank are queried separately; each is authoritative for different facts, and conflicts are resolved on the record.
4. Ask once, then it is policy. A new case type escalates to a human with an evidence pack. The decision becomes a committed policy rule plus test, captured by Entire, and the next similar case resolves itself citing that rule.
One-line tagline: it doesn't say done until it can prove it.
Tooling
Build with Claude Code in your terminal, with Entire hooked in. It is allowed: the rules restrict when code is written (during the hackathon, with dated commits), not which AI tools write it, and Claude Code is one of the agents Entire captures natively. Your editor (VS Code or Cursor) is just for reading diffs.
cfo.ai is not an IDE. It is the business-planning tool (its agent is called Ari) you use near the end to produce the pricing, cost, revenue and runway plan.

Role in Receipts

Writes the code; also the runtime "policy writer" that turns a human decision into a rule + test + commit

Entire

Checkpoints + entire-graph output in the repo
neatlogs
Traces every agent run; detections flag failed tool calls and unproven success claims; prompt versions promoted by label for v1 → v2

AO (Agent Orchestrator)
Spawns parallel Claude Code agents for simulator, verifier and agent core in separate worktrees. Hard cap: 2 hours to get working, else drop

n/a
Set-up order: repo → entire enable --agent claude-code → pip install neatlogs + neatlogs.init() → neathack skill for hackathon.md → first commit.
Scope fence
One complaint type, done deeply. Anything not on the In list waits until after submission.
In
• One complaint type: debited but not credited
• Simulated sender bank, switch and beneficiary bank, with chaos injection (timeouts, connection errors, statuses that change mid-run, a reversal that reports success but does not apply)
• Resolution paths: credited (send proof), failed (reverse, then verify), conflicting or over limit (escalate)
• Receipt verifier with freshness check
• Ask-once escalation that becomes a committed policy rule
• A CLI or bare web page that shows complaint in, reply out, receipts attached
Out
• Real bank or switch APIs
• A polished inbox UI
• Other complaint types, voice, multiple languages
• Pending-and-recheck scheduling (the agent says it is pending, with proof, and stops)
• Auth, users, deployment beyond what the demo needs
Architecture
The agent talks to three simulated sources; every draft reply passes the verifier, and a new case type loops through one human decision that becomes a committed rule.
Repo layout: sim/ (ledger, switch, beneficiary, chaos), agent/ (core loop, tools, prompts), verifier/ (claim schema, span match, freshness), policy/ (committed rules + tests), scenarios/ (30 seeds), evidence/ (screenshots, numbers), hackathon.md.
Workstreams
Six workstreams. W1 to W3 can run in parallel; W4 needs W1 and W3; W5 needs W4; W6 runs throughout.

Entire CLI is an open-source tool from the entireio organization. It hooks into Git to record AI agent sessions and ties them to your commits. The official repository is github.com/entireio/cli. Several other GitHub repos show the same README text, so use the official one.

**Install options**

- **Homebrew (macOS/Linux):** `brew tap entireio/tap` then `brew install --cask entire`. The newer README also offers a nightly build via `entire@nightly`.
- **Install script:** `curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash`
- **Windows:** Scoop, using the entireio scoop-bucket.
- **Go:** `go install github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire@latest`. The README lists this as the development or manual route.

**Setup in a repo**

Run `entire enable` inside your project. The README says this installs agent and git hooks and lets you pick which agents to enable. To enable one agent without the prompt, use `entire enable --agent <name>`, such as `--agent cursor`. Then `entire status` shows the current session state.

**How checkpoints work**

Checkpoints are created on git commits, whether you make them or the agent does. Entire never commits to your active branch. Session metadata goes to a separate `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, so your main history stays clean. The default strategy is manual-commit. An auto-commit strategy snapshots after each agent response instead.

**Supported agents**

Claude Code and Gemini CLI are the most consistently named. Newer README versions also list OpenCode, Cursor, Factory AI Droid, Copilot CLI, and Codex.

**Resuming and rewinding**

- `entire session resume <branch>` restores the latest checkpointed session metadata for a branch.
- Rewind is `entire rewind` in the newest README. Older versions used `entire checkpoint rewind`, which the README now marks as deprecated and slated for removal.

**Version notes**

The package listings show frequent releases, from v0.4.3 in February 2026 to v0.5.4 in April 2026. Command names and install options have changed between versions, so check the README for the version you install. The project is MIT-licensed and currently supports macOS and Linux (via WSL), per one third-party summary.

# Receipts

**It doesn't say done until it can prove it.**

Receipts resolves "debited but not credited" complaints end to end, and is not allowed to tell the customer anything it cannot prove from a trace span.

## The four rules

1. **Every claim needs a receipt.** Each factual claim in an outgoing reply points to the tool span that proves it. A deterministic verifier blocks the send otherwise.
2. **Receipts expire.** A claim about a balance or status is only valid if its read happened after the last action that could have changed it.
3. **Sources disagree, the agent decides who to trust.** Sender bank, switch and beneficiary bank are queried separately; conflicts are resolved on the record.
4. **Ask once, then it is policy.** A new case type escalates to a human; the decision becomes a committed policy rule plus test.

## Layout

| Dir | What |
|---|---|
| `sim/` | Simulated sender ledger, switch, beneficiary bank, chaos layer |
| `agent/` | Core loop, tools, prompts |
| `verifier/` | Claim schema, span match, freshness check |
| `policy/` | Committed rules + tests (written by the ask-once loop) |
| `scenarios/` | 30 seeded complaint scenarios |
| `evidence/` | Screenshots, numbers |
| `hackathon.md` | Build log, failure taxonomy, evidence links |

## Setup

```bash
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/Scripts/activate   # Windows Git Bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

# Built-in browser

The built-in browser is a real browser pane inside the Claude desktop app, separate from the person's Chrome. Its tools are named `mcp__Claude_Browser__*` when the session itself runs inside the desktop app, and `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` when the session runs in the cloud (started from the web, a phone, or the desktop app) and is linked to the person's computer. The names after the prefix are the same either way, Claude uses whichever prefix is actually present, and this skill refers to the tools by the part after the prefix.

If the only built-in browser tool present is `enable__mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser`, Claude calls it first: it turns the built-in browser on for this conversation, and the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__*` tools appear once it has run.

## What the person can see

The browser pane shares the desktop app's side panel with artifacts, documents, and file previews, and the panel shows one of them at a time. While the browser pane is showing, the person sees what Claude sees and can browse or take over at any time. While something else is open in the panel, or the panel is closed, the built-in browser keeps working but the person cannot see it.

Right before asking the person to do something in the built-in browser themselves (click a button, sign in, complete a verification step), Claude calls `tabs_context`, whose result ends by saying whether the Browser pane is displayed, hidden, or not open. If the pane is not open, Claude opens the page first and checks again. If the pane is hidden, Claude first asks the person to bring the browser back in the Claude desktop app: press Cmd+Shift+B on Mac or Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows, or close whatever else is open in the side panel and click the globe icon (the Browser button). Claude then says what to do in the browser. Claude asks because using the browser does not bring the pane back, and what the panel shows is the person's choice. Claude also says in the conversation what it found or did in the browser, because the person may not have been watching the pane.

## Sign-ins persist, and they are the person's

The built-in browser keeps its own persistent profile, shared across the desktop app's sessions. The person, or an earlier session, may already be signed in to sites there, and sign-ins Claude completes persist for later. Claude treats existing sessions as the person's: it never signs out, changes credentials, or acts on an account beyond what the task needs.

## Tabs

The built-in browser has tabs. `preview_start` with a `url` opens an additional tab at that URL in one call and returns a `tabId`, leaving existing tabs untouched, so Claude prefers it over `tabs_create` followed by `navigate` when the destination is already known. `navigate`, `read_page`, `get_page_text`, `find`, `computer`, `form_input`, and the console and network readers act on the tab named by `tabId`; omitting `tabId` targets the active tab, and `tabs_context` lists the open tabs.

## Loading via ToolSearch

Claude loads the built-in browser tools in bulk, not one-by-one: if they are in the deferred list, Claude loads them all in a single ToolSearch call whose query is their full name prefix, for example `{ query: "mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__", max_results: 64 }`.

## Reading pages

Claude prefers `get_page_text` and `read_page` over screenshots for reading, because they return the page's actual text and structure rather than pixels of the visible viewport. `computer` with action "screenshot" is for when the visual layout is the point or the person asks to see the page.

## Site approvals, blocked sites, and request_access

Depending on the person's approval settings, the person may be asked to approve a site before Claude acts on it, and some sites are blocked outright. Claude waits for a pending approval rather than working around it. If a page is refused or an approval is declined, Claude tells the person and moves on rather than retrying.

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, approvals can be answered from any of the person's devices and may take a moment to arrive, and the session may also have a `request_access` tool. If a browser tool answers that the site is not allowed yet and `request_access` is present, Claude calls it with that site's URL and scope "once" (or "site" when the task will keep using that site), waits for the person's answer, and then retries the original tool. Without `request_access`, a refused site is handled as above: Claude tells the person and moves on.

## What the built-in browser cannot open

The built-in browser cannot open `file://` URLs or `localhost` servers that Claude starts itself, because those run where Claude's shell runs, which is not where the browser pane runs. To show the person HTML that Claude generated, Claude uses an artifact instead.

## When the built-in browser cannot be reached

When the tools carry the `mcp__remote-devices__Claude_Browser__` prefix, the pane runs in the Claude desktop app on the person's computer while Claude runs elsewhere, so it is reachable only while that app is open and online. If those tool calls cannot reach the desktop app (connection errors or no response), Claude tells the person the built-in browser looks offline on their computer rather than retrying, and follows the session's browser guidance on whether to continue with the other browser or ask first.

"""A harder chaos profile over the same 30 seeds, derived only from the seed.

The catalog keeps its own light chaos. Stress adds faults a careless agent trips on:
first-call timeouts it should retry, reversals that report success and do not post,
and a switch whose first read is stale. Same seed, same faults, every run.
"""

import random
from dataclasses import replace

from sim.constants import READ_OPS
from sim.models import ChaosFlags, Scenario


def stress_flags(scenario: Scenario) -> ChaosFlags:
    rng = random.Random(f"stress:{scenario.seed}")
    base = scenario.chaos
    flaky = tuple(op for op in READ_OPS if rng.random() < 0.18 and op not in base.timeout_ops)
    lying = base.lying_reversal or (scenario.pattern == "failed_unreversed" and rng.random() < 0.5)
    stale = base.stale_switch_status
    if stale is None and scenario.facts.switch_status != "pending" and rng.random() < 0.25:
        stale = "pending"
    return replace(base, flaky_ops=flaky, lying_reversal=lying, stale_switch_status=stale)


def stressed(scenario: Scenario) -> Scenario:
    return replace(scenario, chaos=stress_flags(scenario))

v1 is a reasonable first attempt with no rules of evidence. It is not told to skip

You are Receipts, a support agent at a Nigerian bank. A customer says their account
was debited for a transfer but the beneficiary was not credited.

Investigate with the tools, then resolve the case:
- If the transfer failed and the customer was debited, reverse the debit.
- If the amount is over NGN 1,000,000.00, escalate to a human instead of acting.
- If the records disagree, escalate to a human.

Finish by calling send_reply. Every claim in the reply cites the receipt_id of the
tool result it is based on. Write short, plain, polite sentences for the customer.
Amounts in tool results are in kobo (100 kobo = NGN 1).

Rules of evidence. A verifier checks your reply against these before it is sent.

1. A write is not a read. sender_reverse returns an acknowledgement, not proof.
   To tell the customer a reversal posted, read the debit again after reversing and
   cite that read (assertion reversal_posted). To say only that you asked for it,
   use reversal_requested.
2. Receipts expire. A claim about the debit, the reversal or the balance must cite
   a read made after your last write.
3. Each source is authoritative for its own facts: the sender ledger for the debit,
   reversal and balance; the switch for the transfer instruction; the beneficiary
   bank for whether the credit posted. If the switch says pending, or the switch and
   the beneficiary disagree, read the switch once more before deciding. Its status

4. If a read fails with timeout or connection_error, retry it once. If it fails

5. If a reversal was accepted but the ledger still shows the debit open, do not

6. Before you act, call policy_lookup with the case type. If a committed rule

7. If send_reply is blocked you get the reasons. Fix the claims, usually by reading

"""Committed policy rules. Each rule is one JSON file a human decision produced.

Rules live in policy/rules/*.json and are read fresh on every lookup, so a rule
committed by the ask-once loop applies to the very next case.
"""

import json
from pathlib import Path

RULES_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "rules"

CASE_TYPES = (
    "credited",
    "failed_unreversed",
    "failed_reversed",
    "switch_success_no_credit",
    "switch_failed_but_credited",
    "over_limit",
    "reversal_not_posted",
    "pending",
    "unknown",
)


def load_rules(rules_dir: Path = RULES_DIR) -> list[dict]:
    rules = []
    for path in sorted(rules_dir.glob("*.json")):
        rule = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        rule["file"] = path.name
        rules.append(rule)
    return rules


def lookup(case_type: str, rules_dir: Path = RULES_DIR) -> dict:
    matches = [r for r in load_rules(rules_dir) if r.get("case_type") == case_type]
    if not matches:
        return {"found": False, "case_type": case_type,
                "note": "No committed rule. If you cannot resolve this on the evidence, escalate."}
    rule = matches[-1]
    return {"found": True, **{k: rule[k] for k in ("rule_id", "case_type", "decision", "instructions",
                                                    "customer_line", "decided_by", "source_case")
                              if k in rule}}

"""Run the model-driven agent over the 30 seeds and compare versions.

    python -m agent.bench run --version v1 --profile stress
    python -m agent.bench run --version v2 --profile stress
    python -m agent.bench summary runs/v1-stress.jsonl runs/v2-stress.jsonl
"""

import argparse
import json
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path

import neatlogs

from agent.tracing import init_tracing
from sim.catalog import load_scenarios
from sim.stress import stress_flags

RUNS = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "runs"


def parse_seeds(text: str) -> list[int]:
    seeds: list[int] = []
    for part in text.split(","):
        if "-" in part:
            lo, hi = part.split("-")
            seeds.extend(range(int(lo), int(hi) + 1))
        elif part:
            seeds.append(int(part))
    return seeds


def run(version: str, profile: str, seeds: list[int], workers: int, out: Path) -> list[dict]:
    from agent.llm import make_client
    from agent.llm_agent import run_case

    init_tracing(tags=[f"prompt:{version}", f"chaos:{profile}"])
    client = make_client()
    scenarios = [s for s in load_scenarios() if s.seed in seeds]

    def one(scenario):
        chaos = stress_flags(scenario) if profile == "stress" else None
        try:
            record = run_case(scenario, version, chaos=chaos, client=client)
        except Exception as exc:  # a crashed run is a result too
            record = {"seed": scenario.seed, "version": version, "status": "crashed", "error": repr(exc)}
        record["profile"] = profile
        print(_line(record), flush=True)
        return record

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers) as pool:
        records = sorted(pool.map(one, scenarios), key=lambda r: r["seed"])
    neatlogs.flush()
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text("".join(json.dumps(r) + "\n" for r in records), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {out}")
    return records


def _line(r: dict) -> str:
    if r.get("status") == "crashed":
        return f"seed={r['seed']:02d} CRASHED {r.get('error')}"
    a = r["audit"]
    flags = []
    if a["false_claims"]:
        flags.append(f"FALSE x{len(a['false_claims'])}")
    if r["unproven_claims_sent"]:
        flags.append(f"unproven x{r['unproven_claims_sent']}")
    if a["harmful_action"]:
        flags.append("HARMFUL")
    if r["blocks"]:
        flags.append(f"blocked x{r['blocks']}")
    ok = "ok " if a["resolved_correctly"] else "BAD"
    return (f"seed={r['seed']:02d} {ok} {r['status']:<8} expected={a['expected']:<8} "
            f"tools={len(r['tool_order'])} ${r['usage']['cost_usd']:.4f} {' '.join(flags)}")


def load(path: Path) -> list[dict]:
    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines() if line.strip()]


def metrics(records: list[dict]) -> dict:
    done = [r for r in records if r.get("status") != "crashed"]
    n = len(records)
    cost = sum(r["usage"]["cost_usd"] for r in done)
    return {
        "runs": n,
        "crashed": n - len(done),
        "resolved_correctly": sum(r["audit"]["resolved_correctly"] for r in done),
        "replies_sent": sum(r["status"] == "sent" for r in done),
        "false_claims_sent": sum(len(r["audit"]["false_claims"]) for r in done),
        "runs_with_false_claim": sum(bool(r["audit"]["false_claims"]) for r in done),
        "unproven_claims_sent": sum(r["unproven_claims_sent"] for r in done),
        "harmful_actions": sum(r["audit"]["harmful_action"] for r in done),
        "debits_left_open_silently": sum(
            r["audit"]["debit_left_open"] and not r.get("escalation") for r in done),
        "replies_blocked_then_fixed": sum(r["blocks"] > 0 and r["status"] == "sent" for r in done),
        "tool_calls_avg": round(sum(len(r["tool_order"]) for r in done) / max(len(done), 1), 1),
        "cost_usd_total": round(cost, 4),
        "cost_usd_per_case": round(cost / max(len(done), 1), 5),
        "latency_s_avg": round(sum(r["latency_s"] for r in done) / max(len(done), 1), 1),
    }


def summary(paths: list[Path]) -> str:
    cols = {p.stem: metrics(load(p)) for p in paths}
    keys = list(next(iter(cols.values())))
    lines = ["| metric | " + " | ".join(cols) + " |", "|---|" + "---|" * len(cols)]
    for k in keys:
        lines.append(f"| {k} | " + " | ".join(str(c[k]) for c in cols.values()) + " |")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def main() -> None:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)
    r = sub.add_parser("run")
    r.add_argument("--version", choices=["v1", "v2"], required=True)
    r.add_argument("--profile", choices=["catalog", "stress"], default="stress")
    r.add_argument("--seeds", default="1-30")
    r.add_argument("--workers", type=int, default=4)
    r.add_argument("--out", type=Path)
    s = sub.add_parser("summary")
    s.add_argument("paths", nargs="+", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    if args.cmd == "run":
        out = args.out or RUNS / f"{args.version}-{args.profile}.jsonl"
        run(args.version, args.profile, parse_seeds(args.seeds), args.workers, out)
    else:
        print(summary(args.paths))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

import json
from types import SimpleNamespace

from agent.llm_agent import run_case
from agent.receipts import ReceiptBook
from tests.helpers import BY_SEED
from verifier.assertions import Claim, check_claim, verify_reply


class ScriptedClient:
    """Each step sees the tool results so far and returns the next tool calls."""

    def __init__(self, steps):
        self.steps = list(steps)
        self.chat = SimpleNamespace(completions=SimpleNamespace(create=self._create))
        self.n = 0

    def _create(self, **kwargs):
        results = [json.loads(m["content"]) for m in kwargs["messages"] if m["role"] == "tool"]
        calls = self.steps.pop(0)(results)
        tool_calls = []
        for name, args in calls:
            self.n += 1
            tool_calls.append(SimpleNamespace(
                id=f"call_{self.n}",
                function=SimpleNamespace(name=name, arguments=json.dumps(args)),
            ))
        message = SimpleNamespace(content=None, tool_calls=tool_calls)
        return SimpleNamespace(choices=[SimpleNamespace(message=message)],
                               usage=SimpleNamespace(prompt_tokens=1000, completion_tokens=100))


def rid(results, op, nth=-1):
    return [r for r in results if r.get("op") == op][nth]["receipt_id"]


TXN = {"transfer_id": "TXN-0028"}

REVERSE = lambda _: [("sender_reverse", TXN)]

    "claims": [{"assertion": "reversal_posted", "receipt_id": rid(r, "sender.reverse"), "value": None,
                "text": "Your reversal has been processed."}],
    "next_step": "Thank you for your patience."})]

             "text": "We asked your bank to reverse the debit."},
            {"assertion": "debit_open", "receipt_id": rid(r, "sender.get_debit"), "value": None,

    client = ScriptedClient([

def attach_as_current(span: otel_trace.Span, *, force_owned: bool = False):
    """
    Make ``span`` the neatlogs *active parent* and return the context token.

    In the DEFAULT single-provider mode this makes ``span`` the OpenTelemetry
    active span so child operations nest correctly: provider auto-instrumentation
    spans, user ``@span`` decorators, ``trace()`` blocks, and ``log()`` LogRecords
    all resolve their parent via the standard OTel active-span context
    (``trace.get_current_span()`` / ``set_span_in_context``).

    In ISOLATED mode (init(tracer_provider=<private>)) it does NOT overwrite the
    global current-span. It instead records ``span`` under a PRIVATE context key
    that only neatlogs reads. This keeps a co-tenant instrumentor (openlit /
    langfuse) resolving its parent from the HOST's current-span — so foreign
    spans never nest under a neatlogs span, and neatlogs spans never borrow a
    foreign parent. neatlogs' own children still nest correctly because
    ``get_tracer()`` resolves their parent from this same private key.

    Detach the returned token (in a ``finally``) when the span completes.

        token = attach_as_current(span)
        try:
            ...
        finally:
            context_api.detach(token)
    """
    is_nl = force_owned or _is_neatlogs_span(span)
    if _isolation_active():
        # ISOLATED: thread the neatlogs parent privately; leave the global
        # current-span untouched so foreign instrumentation nests under the host.
        ctx = set_neatlogs_span_in_context(span, force_owned=force_owned)
        return context_api.attach(ctx)

    ctx = otel_trace.set_span_in_context(span)
    # Mark that a neatlogs span is active in this context subtree. A foreign
    # instrumentation (e.g. openlit) may push its OWN spans as the immediate
    # current span BETWEEN two neatlogs spans (crew kickoff → openlit agent span →
    # our llm.call). Inspecting only the immediate current span would then mistake
    # the openlit span for "no neatlogs parent" and detach our child into its own
    # trace, fragmenting the crew. This flag records that a neatlogs ancestor
    # exists somewhere up the active chain, so the root-guard nests instead of
    # detaching. Context is immutable+nested, so the flag scopes to the subtree.
    if is_nl:
        ctx = context_api.set_value(_NEATLOGS_ACTIVE_KEY, True, ctx)
    return context_api.attach(ctx)
